note: Original description (as Nasutitermes bragantinus), soldier only; the original states that the alate and the worker are unknown. The genus was later combined as Rotunditermes. The text is OCR of a library scan.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: (Placed in the genus Nasutitermes in the original.) Head pale brown; nasus darker, paler at the tip; antenna yellowish brown; thoracic tergites, legs and abdomen brown. Head with a few longer hairs; nasus tip with several short hairs. Abdomen more hairy, with short and slightly longer hairs. Body length including the nasus 3.2—3.4 mm. Head capsule nearly circular, the posterior margin nearly straight; head length 1.53—1.63 mm greater than the maximum width 0.95—1.00 mm. Nasus short, slender, nearly cylindrical, about half the length of the rest of the head capsule. Mandible tips not visible from above. Fontanelle and fontanelle gland visible. In lateral view the anterodorsal region of the head capsule bears a slight swelling followed by a shallow depression. Antenna 13 segments, fairly hairy: segment 1 long, thick, cylindrical; segment 2 about half of segment 1; segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2; segment 4 the smallest; segment 5 about as long as segment 3 and far longer than segment 4; segments 6 to the last gradually longer. Labrum whitish translucent, band-shaped, about 2 times as wide as long, the anterior margin convex, the anterolateral corners rounded. Anteclypeus transparent, band-shaped, far wider than long, the middle of the anterior margin slightly projecting. Postclypeus far wider than the anteclypeus, with several stout hairs, the anterior margin concave, the posterior margin rounded and convex. Mandibles small, reduced, each with a lateral toothless spine-like process. Postmentum nearly trapezoidal, slightly wider than long, narrower anteriorly, fairly hairy, both the anterior and the posterior margin nearly straight. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, wider than long, with a few long and short hairs on both margins; anterior margin nearly straight, with a weak notch in the middle; posterior margin slightly convex, without a median notch. Mesonotum narrower than the pronotum, metanotum about as wide as the pronotum, both with a convex posterior margin without a median notch. Legs long and slender, with moderate pilosity apart from the tarsi, which bear many hairs and stout spines. Tibial apical spur formula 2:2:2. Tarsi 4-segmented, ending in a pair of claws, without an arolium. Abdomen moderately hairy, with short and long hairs. Cerci short (length 0.09 mm), 2-segmented, hairy. No styli. For measurements see the table (Roonwal and Rathore, table 2, columns 4 and 5).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate and worker unknown. Type material: the soldier holotype (Z. S. I. Reg. No. 17/H11) in the Zoological Survey of India (Calcutta); 2 soldier paratypes in the Museu de Zoologia da Universidade de São Paulo, and another 2 soldiers (together with 3 damaged ones) and 5 slide preparations in the Z. S. I. Type locality and distribution: only the type locality is known, the Bragantina region, Pará, Brazil (Tube No. 20, Fd. Coll. No. 8; 9 soldiers, collected by E. Sefer in 1956). Closely related to N. major, from which it differs in its smaller size (body length 4.4—5.1 mm, this being the comparison text for the worker), pale brown head capsule, indistinct fontanelle and weakly saddle-shaped pronotum. The genus combination is Rotunditermes bragantinus.
